newsitem.title: USA: U.S. discussing security with Baltic states.
newsitem.headline: U.S. discussing security with Baltic states.

text.p: The United States is prepared to negotiate a security pact with Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia to keep them from feeling isolated by the proposed expansion of NATO, a White House spokesman said on Friday.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said there have been ongoing discussions about the prospective accord, whose purpose would be to advance the integration of the three Baltic states into the trans-Atlantic community.

"We've got a number of initiatives that we are pursuing with them -- bilateral, regional. ... We have discussed with them some type of joint document that would outline some of the shared commitments that we have to sovereignty, independence and security within the Baltics," McCurry said.

The issue of how to preserve Baltic security has become part of President Bill Clinton's foreign policy agenda in the aftermath of the Helsinki summit, where Russian President Boris Yeltsin reluctantly agreed in principle to the inclusion of former Communist Warsaw Pact countries in NATO.

Russian officials have said they would vigorously oppose extending NATO membership to countries that were once part of the Soviet Union, and the U.S.-led alliance has made no commitments to Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia, which regained their independence when the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991.

NATO leaders will meet in Madrid in July to extend the first invitations to former East Bloc countries to join. Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are expected to be among the first countries admitted.
A U.S. security agreement with the Baltics "would not be any substitution or compensation for the eventual question of whether these Baltic states want to become members of NATO," McCurry said.

"Membership is open to them because membership in NATO is non-exclusionary, as we said repeatedly. That's an issue that would be addressed by the alliance as we move ahead on the question of expansion."

Many Americans trace their ancestry to the Baltic states, giving Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia a good deal of U.S. political clout. New York Republic Representative Gerald Solomon is currently circulating a resolution in Congress that calls on the Clinton administration to back NATO membership for them.
